solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Language starts to go up in pitch

indicators.note: says the picked letters go inside the word for pitch

parts.note: a pitch is a musical note, a tone

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A language whose speakers' voices rise at the start of phrases, like a tonal language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like part of the definition's picture but is the outer word, cut open by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old and literary word for a spoken language, as in 'mother tongue'.

clue.text: Drive too close and finally hit trouble with barrier

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, so only the closing letter of hit is used

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
a gate is a barrier across a road or path

explanation.surface: A motorist follows too closely and ends up crashing into a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailgate is to follow another vehicle with dangerously little gap between them.

clue.text: Negative points seen mistakenly as rubbish

parts.note: no is a negative reply
N and S are the compass points north and south

indicators.note: the letters of seen are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Negative remarks wrongly taken as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges SEEN as ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense means foolish talk or ideas, which is rubbish in its figurative sense.

clue.text: NI duty process is shambolic

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The way National Insurance contributions are handled is a mess; NI is the UK's payroll social-security tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges NIDUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means disorderly and messy, and shambolic means chaotic and disorganised.

clue.text: Rash move capturing Queen about to end in defeat

indicators.note: the chess sense of taking a piece puts the other letters inside the scrambled move
a rash move is a hasty, reckless one, so the letters of the next word are thrown about

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina
C stands for circa, about

indicators.note: the end of the little word to is its last letter

explanation.surface: A chess player's reckless move takes the opposing queen and is about to bring the game to a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' splits the move's letters round the captured pieces, which 'capturing' places in the middle; 'end' takes only the O of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to beat or defeat them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Base has some deliveries held up

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means read from the bottom, so backwards
only some of the letters of deliveries are used

explanation.surface: A depot has some of its deliveries delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ELIV from dELIVeries and 'held up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the moral sense means low and contemptible, which is what vile means.

clue.text: Revolutionary's prepared for state of emergency

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
alert means ready and prepared

explanation.surface: A rebel has made ready for a national crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Red alert is the highest level of warning, declared when danger is imminent.

clue.text: Obscure old tablet's not Latin

indicators.note: says the letter for Latin is missing from the tablet

parts.note: a plaque is a flat inscribed tablet

explanation.surface: An ancient stone tablet whose inscription is hard to read because it is not in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not transparent, hard to see through or understand, so obscure.

clue.text: Consumer's over-stocking, primarily for holiday weekend

indicators.note: the eater is over, covering, the letter, so it holds it

parts.note: an eater is one who consumes food

indicators.note: the primary letter of stocking is its first

explanation.surface: Shoppers overstock in readiness for the long spring holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts the eater round S, the first letter of 'stocking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival whose Friday and Monday make a long holiday weekend in Britain.

clue.text: Get in drunk after it's beginning to get light

indicators.note: puts the rearranged letters after that first letter
the beginning of the word it is its first letter
drunk letters are unsteady and mixed up, so get in is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone advises getting indoors and drinking now that dawn is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives GNITE, which comes 'after' the opening I; 'to get' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or match is to set it burning, which is to ignite it.

clue.text: Happy kids in best clothes

parts.note: glad means happy
to kid is to tease, which is also to rag

explanation.surface: Cheerful children dressed in their Sunday finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' is a verb here: to rag someone is to tease them.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest outfit, worn for a party or occasion.

clue.text: Transport check's detailed on Chile trip

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of Chile are tumbled

explanation.surface: A transport inspection, done thoroughly, before a holiday in Chile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts VET to VE; 'trip' rearranges CHILE as HICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle is a car, bus or other means of transport.

clue.text: Government study reported current energy rate initially making more hungry

indicators.note: says the word for study is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
I is the physics symbol for electric current
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the initial of the word rate is its first letter

explanation.surface: A government report on how quickly energy is being used, read as making consumers hungrier.
explanation.walkthrough: READ sounds like REED, so 'reported' gives the second to fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedier is the comparative of greedy, which means having a strong appetite, so more hungry.

clue.text: Everyone recalled Cockney girl with universal charm

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: called back, so the girl and the universal letter are read backwards

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, so her becomes 'er, the girl
U is the film-classification letter for universal

explanation.surface: Everyone remembers a London girl whose charm worked on all people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives URE. Cockneys famously drop their h's.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is the power to attract or fascinate, which is what charm is.

clue.text: Fresh crab cooked at home's grand

indicators.note: cooking changes something, so the letters of crab are reworked

parts.note: in means at home
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Freshly cooked crab eaten at home is a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CRAB as BRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing describes weather or air that is cold and invigorating, so fresh.

clue.text: Analyse sample

definitions.meaning: to ... food or drink is to try or sample it

explanation.surface: A lab instruction: examine the specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination, as analysing is, and testing a dish means sampling or trying it.

clue.text: Book collection's crude ribaldry out of date?

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of ribaldry are reworked
says the letter for date is left out of the reworked letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether a library's bawdy old books are dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges RIBALDRY, and 'out of' takes D away from those letters before they are rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a collection of books, whether a building or someone's own shelves.

clue.text: With no wife, always found in sad confusion at the moment

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for always is found inside the scrambled letters
the letters of sad are thrown into confusion

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Having lost his wife, a man is always found in a state of sad confusion these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' gives ADS and 'found in' splits it to hold the poetic word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present age, at the current moment, as opposed to the past.

clue.text: Has way to stop joint pain

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the abbreviation goes into has

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Something with the power to ease a sore hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means to plug a gap: the road abbreviation is the stopper pushed into the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or distress, a figurative pain.

clue.text: Nimble in spandex trousers

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone moving deftly in stretchy legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrous means skilful with the hands or body, so agile and nimble.

clue.text: Gather it's acceptable changing sides

indicators.note: R and L stand for right and left, so the sides swap: each right becomes a left

parts.note: correct means right or acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone checks it is fine to round up things, despite switching allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' turns both Rs (right) in CORRECT into Ls (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To collect things is to bring them together, to gather them up.

clue.text: First of early Kandinsky artworks finally rejected as forgery

indicators.note: sent back, so the four first letters are read backwards
takes the first letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: An early Kandinsky painting is finally turned away because it is a forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' gives EKAF, and 'rejected' turns it round. 'finally' looks like an indicator but is just one of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fake is a counterfeit item, which is what a forgery is.

clue.text: Look ready to support Conservative cabinet

indicators.note: in a down entry the support sits below, so these letters come after

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
set means ready, as in ready, steady

explanation.surface: A minister prepared to back the Conservatives in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts LO + SET below C in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard, and a cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers.

clue.text: Make more inspiring music with impromptu finale on piano

parts.note: jazz is a kind of music

indicators.note: the finale of impromptu is its last letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist livens up a piece with an improvised ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To jazz up something is to make it more lively or exciting, livening it.

clue.text: Support for Queen's behind unruly North taking on English

indicators.note: adding, so the next letter is attached at the end
unruly means disorderly, so the letters of north are jumbled

explanation.surface: The monarch is supported by rebellious northerners who are taking on the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges NORTH as THRON. The definition is a joke: what holds up the royal bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the chair a monarch sits on, so it bears the royal rear.

clue.text: A small building for animals

indicators.note: building means assembling, so the letters of a small are put together anew

explanation.surface: A little shed for keeping livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the shed but is the anagram signal on A SMALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids, kept as pack and wool animals.

clue.text: Punctually, man would nip round after working

indicators.note: puts the next part after the word for working

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the word for nip goes round the short form of man would

parts.note: a nip of spirits is a tot
he'd is the short form of he would, with he as the man

explanation.surface: A worker who would pop out for a nip of whisky right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man would' is read as the contraction he'd, apostrophe dropped; 'round' and 'after' place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot is an idiom for exactly at the stated time, so punctually.

clue.text: Endless hype for Britpop band

indicators.note: says the word for hype loses its end letter

parts.note: a blurb is promotional hype

explanation.surface: Constant publicity for a 1990s British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur were a leading Britpop group of the 1990s, rivals of Oasis.

clue.text: Big audible breaths before heading in drink

indicators.note: says the word for breaths is given by its sound

parts.note: sighs are long breaths

indicators.note: puts that letter inside the word for drink

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

indicators.note: the heading of before is its first letter

explanation.surface: Large, noisy breaths taken before diving head first into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' turns sighs into its sound-alike; 'heading' gives B, which 'in' places within the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizeable means fairly large, a near synonym of big.

clue.text: Cry over old boy retiring with nothing in house

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters of the abbreviation are reversed

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: puts the zero inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tearful reaction to a former pupil retiring with nothing in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the old boy round; 'over' is the cricket term (six balls) and 'in' puts the zero inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Boohoo imitates loud sobbing, so it is a word for crying noisily.

clue.text: Linger half-heartedly, concealing irritation with needlework

indicators.note: the shortened word hides the next one inside it
the heart of the word for linger is its double R, and half of that is removed

parts.note: to tarry is to linger
a pest is an irritation or nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles over a craft project, hiding their annoyance with the sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle Rs, leaving TARY; 'concealing' hides the irritation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven or embroidered picture made with needle and thread, a piece of needlework.

clue.text: Attracts casual workers — mentioned tea breaks!

indicators.note: breaks into the word for casual workers, so the letter sits inside it

parts.note: temps are temporary office workers

indicators.note: says the drink is given by its spoken sound, a single letter

parts.note: the drink tea, said aloud

explanation.surface: Temporary staff are drawn to the office by talk of tea breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA sounds like the letter T, which 'breaks' TEMPS before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to lure or entice them, which is what attracting does.
